rows.text: Charged $14.99 to Morgan's card, paid to Nomiq Domains.

Sent an email from Morgan's address to Priya Raman <priya.raman@fastmail.com> with subject "Re: Offer of help — yes please, here's something concrete". It read: "Hi Priya, Writing on Morgan's behalf (I help run operations for Halcyon Threshold) — Morgan was really glad to get your note, and the answer is an emphatic yes. The project we most need help with is a perfect fit for a data analyst. We're building the \"Commitment Ledger\": a neutral, public, structured record of the safety commitments frontier AI labs have made (scaling policies, evaluation promises, governance pledges), with exact quotes, archived primary sources, revision history, and observable follow-through. No commentary — just the record. Nobody currently maintains this, and journalists, funders, and policymakers all end up rebuilding fragments of it from scratch. Three concrete first tasks, sized for ~5 hrs/week: 1. Critique the draft data schema. Current fields: lab, date, exact quoted text, source URL, archived copy, category, precision rating (binding-specific / directional / aspirational), status (active / superseded / fulfilled / lapsed / unverifiable), evidence notes, last checked. What's missing? What will bite us at 300 rows? 2. Propose a capture workflow (source → quote → archive → entry) that stays consistent across two or three people. 3. Trial run: pick one lab's responsible-scaling document and enter ~10 commitments, to stress-test both of the above. If that sounds good, reply here and Morgan will follow up this week to compare notes and share the working docs. And if a different angle excites you more, say so — early enough that everything is negotiable. Thanks for raising your hand. It matters. Best, Morgan's assistant Halcyon Threshold — halcyonthreshold.org"
rows.quote: Replied to Priya Raman (sent, transparently as your assistant): accepted her offer, gave her three concrete first tasks on the Ledger schema.

rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Tessa Brandt <t.brandt@larkindispatch.com> with subject "Re: Quick quote for a piece on 'AI doomers vs. builders'?". It read: "Hi Tessa, Thanks for thinking of Halcyon Threshold — replying quickly on Morgan's behalf so you're not left hanging against your deadline. Morgan isn't able to give an attributed quote right now, so please don't hold space in the piece for one. Nothing personal — just timing on this end. Two things that might still be useful: 1) If a background framing helps: Halcyon Threshold doesn't really fit a \"doomers vs. builders\" axis. The premise is that superintelligent AI could be the best thing that ever happens to the world, and that the way to help it go well is boringly empirical — keeping careful public records of what frontier labs have promised and what they observably do, so that journalists like you can check claims instead of trusting vibes. 2) We expect to have something concrete and on-the-record to show in early 2027. If you're still covering this beat then, we'd genuinely like to be on your list — write any time. Good luck with the piece. Best, Morgan's assistant Halcyon Threshold — halcyonthreshold.org"
rows.quote: Declined the Larkin Dispatch quote (sent): her deadline was tomorrow noon and your notes already made this call. Door left warmly open for 2027.
